title: Bernardo Reyes to Ignacio Revueltas, Monterrey, 1 April 1886 (catalogue 1447): War Ministry two-digit key rebuilt from the cipher letter and contemporary translation of 9 Dec 1885 (DLI.3.524.1), tested on a held-out half, and applied to the ten cipher runs of DLI.4.634.1

system.summary: Clear Spanish with key words in two-digit numbers joined by hyphens. Each group stands for one letter; letters have one to three groups (a 17 47 87; e 13 43 83; i 19 49 89; o 21 31 61; r 57 77 97; t 56 76 96). ch appears to have its own groups (12, 82, from context). The War Ministry key of the Reyes-Revueltas channel, not the President's four-digit code nor the new table of 16 Mar 1886.
system.notes: Groups joined by hyphens within a run; runs separated by clear words. Key: 41 groups frozen from 245 pairs of DLI.3.524.1 (key_frozen.tsv). Seven groups of 634.1 (12, 20, 23, 40, 53, 65, 82) are not in it and are filled from context in the reading.

prior_solution.where: No edition or decipherment found: two web searches on 12 Nov 2026 (general work on Reyes and Porfirian espionage only); catalogue check of 28 Oct 2026 (known.py, Narváez articles) found none.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1447) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, built and froze the key, ran the held-out test, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (key build, held-out test, decryption, mark check)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: DLI.4.634.1 and siblings DLI.3.455.1, 3.524.1, 3.525.1, 4.623.1, 4.630.1 fetched from the CEHM image server, one at a time, 2 s apart.

Sign conventions written first; the 68 groups of 634.1 transcribed in two passes (1x, then fresh 2x crops), 68/68 agree. The 634.1 runs were also read tentatively from the clear context before the sibling was fetched.

Key built from the cipher and contemporary translation of DLI.3.524.1 only (245 pairs, 41 groups, no conflicts) and frozen (key_frozen.tsv, FROZEN.sha256). DLI.3.455.1 p. 2 and DLI.3.525.1 checked and found to be in the President's four-digit code, not used.

Held-out: key from rows 1-15 of 524.1 applied to rows 16-31 and graded against the translation: 99 of 114 letters right, 0 wrong, 15 on unseen groups. On 634.1 the frozen key covers 60 of 68 groups and agrees with the earlier context reading on all 60 (agreement, not blind).

634.1 decrypted mechanically with key_frozen.tsv and read with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py rebuilds the decryption and passes. 5 of 12 cipher words verbatim, 7 with one context-filled letter, 0 holes. The reading checker: reading 0.722, letter section 0.818, translation 0.765.
Two web searches: no edition or decipherment of this letter.

Independent blind review by a second AI language-model agent: 50 of the 68 groups of 634.1 and three lines plus one row of 524.1 checked against the images, all agree; check_marks.py, decrypt.py and the held-out test reproduced. The reviewer set the text to not prose (10 short runs inside a clear letter, as ralamb1657), grade B.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 313 tokens, 48 types, es-modern order 4: reading -1.714 per letter; random keys -6.835 (z 9.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.891 (mean -3.02, z 8.8); annealer on the real text -2.615. Verdict: pass.

Integration check (12 Nov 2026): the two sibling translated telegrams the contributor had not used were fetched and decrypted with key_frozen.tsv without changing it. DLI.4.631.1 (Revueltas to Reyes, 24 Mar 1886, 'Clave antigua', translation 'Por correo de hoy escribo a Ud extensamente sobre asunto relativo a colocacion del Sr. Lozano'): 47 letters right, 0 wrong, 14 on groups not in the key. DLI.3.416.1 (28 Oct 1885, translation 'debe decir a la autoridad legal y legitimamente constituida'): 44 right, 0 wrong, 5 not in the key. Together 91 letters right, 0 wrong, 19 unknown. They confirm 23 = n (twice) and 65 = n-tilde, two of the seven groups of 634.1 that rested on context.

Integration check (12 Nov 2026): DLI.4.634.1 image compared with transcription_634.txt (R1, R2, R5, R6, R8 groups and the rest read against the page): agree. FROZEN.sha256 reproduced; key rebuilt from the first rows of transcription_524.txt by hand (row 1 particular = 30 17 77 76 19 16 74 68 87 57) agrees. Strict share recounted: 5 of 12 words = 0.417; fraction_read corrected from 1.0.

Integration check: two more web searches (Reyes/Revueltas clave cifrada 1886 edition; Narváez on Mexican cryptography with Reyes, Garza Galán, Cervantes). Nothing names this letter or key; Narváez 2019 (SRE) and the Ríos Vázquez thesis not opened.

outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from the contemporary translation of the cipher letter DLI.3.524.1 (9 Dec 1885) in the same channel, frozen, tested on a held-out half of that letter, and applied to the bare cipher runs of DLI.4.634.1.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Strict count by the README read bar: 5 of the 12 cipher words (su, miedo, conducta, dejar, eso) are read from the signs with the frozen key; the other 7 each rest on one letter given by the context alone (a group not in the key) and count as not read: 5/12 = 0.417. All 12 words are identified and none is a hole. The contributor's earlier field gave 1.0 (all runs given a value).

texts.label: DLI.4.634.1, Reyes to Revueltas, 1 Apr 1886: 10 cipher runs in a clear letter
texts.summary: Garza Galán, since his arrival, is moving towards a reconciliation with General Cervantes, which shows Reyes how useful his journey to the capital was; but since Reyes fears a 'ranchero' more than a politician, he will keep watch on that gentleman's conduct, without ceasing to draw their relations closer.
texts.note: Not prose: 10 short cipher runs (one or two words each, 12 words) set into a letter written in clear Spanish; given with our decode with key_frozen.tsv and an English gloss. The runs form no sentence of their own; the sentence is carried by the clear text around them. Words: 5 verbatim from the signs (su, miedo, conducta, dejar, eso), 7 with one letter filled from context on a group not in the frozen key (provechoso, viaje, capital, ranchero, pendiente, dicho, señor; 82 = ch holds at both of its places), ranchero also with the writer's dropped a restored. No holes. The cipher words carry Reyes's distrust of Garza Galán; the clear text carries the reconciliation news. Independent blind review (12 Nov 2026): 50 of 68 groups checked against the image, all agree; check_marks and the held-out test reproduced; set to not prose (grade B) on the ralamb1657 rule for short runs inside clear letters.

texts.label: DLI.3.524.1, Revueltas to Reyes, 9 Dec 1885 (key source and held-out test)
texts.note: The key source: each cipher run of the letter decrypted with key_frozen.tsv beside the words of the contemporary translation on page 2 (scripts/decrypt_524.py). Rows tagged '!' (not one group to one letter) are shown but were not used to build the key. No reading of our own is claimed.

gaps.detail: Values from context only (ch, p, j, v, ch). Two of the seven first listed are now confirmed by two other translated telegrams in the same key (DLI.4.631.1 and DLI.3.416.1, integration check 12 Nov 2026): 23 = n and 65 = ñ. Neither letter has any of the five groups left.
The weakest word (raised by the reviewer): the writer's dropped a restored and 12 = ch from context.
